shape_hint: A thick square nut: top view is a square of side s with a central threaded hole (sharp corners across e), side view is a rectangle of height m; sometimes a slightly chamfered circular bearing face of diameter dw on one side.

role_map.s_max: width across flats (square side), nominal = max

notes: Only DIN 557 was checked (also named DIN 562 thin square nut, KS B 1013, ASME B18.2.2 - not verified). DIN 557 itself has two historical widths for M10 (s=17 vs 16) and M12 (s=19 vs 18); the table uses the common s=17 and s=19; the s=16 / s=18 variants appear only in fasten.it and fullerfasteners. Sizes M4 and M20+ are not in DIN 557:1994. row_support = lowest per-column agreement (e_min, m_min and dw_min have exactly 3 sources for some rows).

A fasten.it: fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_557 (P, dw, e max, m, mw, s)

verification.checks_done: Live curl (HTTP 200) of fasten.it, fullerfasteners, digipich, boltsfastener, schrauben-lexikon, nfgab and globalfastener detail_239; JC PDF not used. 6 rows (M5..M16) x 8 columns (P,s_max,e_max,e_min,m_max,m_min,dw_min,mw_min) x 7 page instances: no record cell conflicts with any page value except mw_min on globalfastener's DIN 557-1985 page (2.4/3.1/4.0/5.1/6.4/8.5, older edition, same cluster as fuller which agrees) and fuller M16 m_max typo 'l3'. Clusters per cell (JC PDF excluded): s_max, e_max, m_max 5; P, dw_min, mw_min 3 (fasten.it, fuller/globalfastener, digipich); e_min and m_min 2 (fuller, digipich). Sanity: e_max=1.414*s within 0.1, e_max>e_min, m_max>m_min>mw_min, monotone, pitch=ISO coarse.
problems: e_min and m_min fail: only fullerfasteners and digipich (2 clusters) list them; the producer's third source was the JC Fasteners PDF datasheet, which may only corroborate. Drop both columns (no other independent page found: engineeringhardware e_min is derived, der-schraubenladen is images).

Thin cells (exactly 3 clusters, all 6 rows): P, dw_min, mw_min = fasten.it, fuller(+globalfastener), digipich. digipich shows no shared typos with fuller or fasten.it (fuller's M16 'l3' typo not copied), so it is counted separately; if digipich were found to derive from fuller these three columns would also fail.
boltsfastener and schrauben-lexikon carry the same row layout (d, s, e, m) and the same M4..M16 values -> counted once (producer already counted 6-7 'sources' for s/e/m max; clustered count is 5).

fullerfasteners table 2 column labels are scrambled ('M10 SW 16', 'M12', 'M12 SW 18' hold s=17, 18, 19); rows must be identified by s value, which matches fasten.it/digipich s=17/19 rows - a label inference, harmless for the kept s=17/19 rows.

Row convention: M10 uses s=17 (not the older s=16, dw 14.5, e 22.6) and M12 uses s=19 (not 18); fasten.it/fuller/globalfastener list both widths, digipich/boltsfastener/schrauben-lexikon/nfgab list 17/19. Edition note: globalfastener DIN 557-1985 differs in m/mw from the 1994 table used here (m max 4.6/min 3.4 vs 4/3.52 for M5).
Semantics fine: s_max=nominal=max, e_max=across corners max, m_max=nominal, dw_min=bearing diameter min, mw_min=m1/mw effective wrench height min - all read from headers.

standard_full: DIN 557 (square nuts, product grade C, 1994 table; coarse thread)
